<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-localization"></a>

## Cutoffs, periodization and discrete energy

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_localization.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_localization.esk#L1). SHA-256: `3f42a5ad891e010417e6625ce2921181eefcdfabdfdc72b765f7b70cdbe768ff`.

**Published result:** Section 10 of the reference construction (Proposition 10.1, Lemmas 10.2–10.4, (10.20)–(10.23), Corollary 10.6): the local solution is multiplied by smooth cutoffs to give a compactly supported force, the energy identity holds with the force defined as the residual, and compact support transports the construction to the torus T³ = R³/Z³. The program checks four ingredients: a cutoff that cancels a temporal pole, exact compact support, periodization within one cell, and the discrete energy identity.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Check localization ingredients in explicitly constructed fields.

**Implemented algorithm:** Cancel a temporal pole with a cutoff polynomial, guard spatial bumps, periodize within one cell and differentiate a discrete energy model.

**Domain and parameters:** Source-defined support boxes/radii and period cell; three registered criteria for smooth extension, energy and torus scaling.

**Arithmetic:** Rational finite-grid/cutoff data and AD; the discrete energy equality is asserted exactly.

**Checks in the source:** Support/period-cell agreement, torus averages, exact energy balance and oversized-radius/dropped-viscosity negative controls are asserted.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. The energy balance is a discrete model, not an independently proved continuum energy estimate.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 15, Failed: 0; 1.38 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 15, Failed: 0; compile 1.69 s, run 0.20 s). ## Compact mean corrections and moment solve

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_mean_corrections.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_mean_corrections.esk#L1). SHA-256: `700a0d7391951114ba3f5d0e0da8941f4dc20e92137615b8e4c9541349416944`.

**Published result:** Section 8 of the reference construction (Proposition 8.1 through Lemma 8.8): compactly supported, divergence-free mean corrections are built as curls of compactly supported potentials, and five radial moment conditions (three azimuthal, two axial) are solved with geometric bump copies, which leads to a generalized Vandermonde system. The program verifies div(curl A) = 0 by AD on a piecewise-polynomial compactly supported potential and solves the five-moment system exactly at λ = 1.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Realize selected mean corrections with solved amplitudes.

**Implemented algorithm:** Build supported divergence-free bump fields, compute a five-moment generalized Vandermonde matrix and solve amplitudes with exact_linalg.

**Domain and parameters:** Five moments at λ=1; source-selected disjoint correction boxes and sample points.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational moment system; AD divergence/residual checks as implemented.

**Checks in the source:** Moment realization, support separation, divergence and wrong-support/oversized-cutoff negative controls are asserted.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-oscillatory-realization"></a>

## Auxiliary-torus pulse realization

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_oscillatory_realization.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_oscillatory_realization.esk#L1). SHA-256: `b5aa516b7ce59234db58123cbbcc460971c67a1f17d4619be4ab20092ee0dee3`.

**Published result:** Sections 6–7 and 2.2 of the reference construction: two families of pulses with different ratios of angular-momentum flux to axial-momentum flux are combined so that their averaged quadratic velocity products supply both components of the required leading stress, on an auxiliary torus. The program realizes the mechanism exactly on a four-point auxiliary torus, where cos and sin at kπ/2 are integers, and solves for positive in-cone family weights.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Recover averaged stress from two independent pulse families.

**Implemented algorithm:** Construct trigonometric polynomials on a four-point auxiliary torus, extract zero-mode fluxes and solve a two-component stress matrix.

**Domain and parameters:** Two distinct C/B flux ratios, in-cone target stresses and four-point torus average.

**Arithmetic:** Exact trigonometric representation/torus products and rational exact_linalg solve.

**Checks in the source:** Zero means, distinct flux ratios, full rank two and positive solved weights are asserted; one-family rank-one failures are negative controls.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. The finite auxiliary-torus stress realization is distinct from full spatial oscillatory error estimates.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-pulse-growth"></a>

## Craik–Criminale crossover on simple shear

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_pulse_growth.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_pulse_growth.esk#L1). SHA-256: `3bcbc358e7d3299f0e0ea4e6aec9094ebf21d0961eacfc7abf2aa7a419461813`.

**Published result:** The reference construction's Introduction (citing Craik–Criminale [9], exact finite-amplitude waves on affine background flows) and Section 2.2's description of the pulses: the background shear supplies growth, shortening the radial wavelength raises viscous damping, amplification dominates first and damping later. The program makes the Craik–Criminale wavevector law exact for simple shear and bisects the amplification/damping crossover of a representative growth-rate model to an exact rational bracket.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>
- A. D. D. Craik, W. O. Criminale, "Evolution of wavelike disturbances in shear flows: a class of exact solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations", Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 406 (1986), 13–26 (reference [9] of the construction). <https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1986.0061>

**Purpose:** Compare an amplification/damping crossover with an integrated amplitude curve.

**Implemented algorithm:** Derive the affine-background wavevector law and log-amplitude rate, bisect the crossover and integrate the amplitude by RK4.

**Domain and parameters:** Source-selected simple-shear/viscosity parameters, finite sampled time range and zero-shear negative control.

**Arithmetic:** Exact/rational wavevector and rate checks with AD; RK4/exp comparison uses 1e-3 relative tolerance and one-step peak tolerance.

**Checks in the source:** Derivative/rate agreement, interior maximum and growth-then-decay are asserted; zero shear removes amplification/crossover.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. Finite integration and sampled tails do not by themselves certify every asymptotic statement.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

## Pulse covariance and shear growth

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_pulse_stress.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_pulse_stress.esk#L1). SHA-256: `df6bef6bc9cf6f15debb860401ad08a460ef80981f10cc1b3f2ce72da6a9b42d`.

**Published result:** Sections 2.2, 3.2, 3.3 and 7 of the reference construction: oscillatory ring pulses have zero angular mean but nonzero averaged momentum fluxes ⟨w_r w_θ⟩, ⟨w_r w_z⟩, and two pulse families with different flux ratios represent the required leading stress T = c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ with c₁, c₂ > 0; each pulse grows by shear amplification and then decays once viscosity wins (the Craik–Criminale / Orr mechanism). The program computes the averages, the 2×2 covariance solve, and one pulse mode's growth and decay.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Compute the momentum flux supplied by two oscillatory pulse families.

**Implemented algorithm:** Average angular products, solve a rational two-family covariance system and integrate one transverse mode on an affine background.

**Domain and parameters:** Source-defined two covariance directions and shear-mode trajectory/time grid.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational covariance/positivity checks; trajectory and growth comparisons are numerical.

**Checks in the source:** Zero angular means, nonzero fluxes, transversality, positive solve and interior growth/damping peak checks are asserted.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-residual-ladder"></a>

## Three-rung residual improvement model

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_residual_ladder.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_residual_ladder.esk#L1). SHA-256: `c64df90fbd3fe1ddf54064d2741c781e6e0576d727c24ac2dcc432854432652b`.

**Published result:** Section 9 of the reference construction, (9.8) and (9.18): the residual exponents climb the ladder σ₀ = 1/5, σ_{j+1} = σ_j + 1/10, with B_j = 1/2 + σ_j and C*_j = 1 + σ_j, each correction cycle (Proposition 9.6) raising the order to which the residual vanishes. The program checks the ladder in exact arithmetic and runs three rungs of a scalar model of the correction cycle, cancelling one Taylor coefficient per rung.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Make finite residual improvement and skipped-rung failures explicit.

**Implemented algorithm:** Compute the rational exponent ladder and cancel three Taylor coefficients of the scalar residual with linear term 2w and quadratic w².

**Domain and parameters:** Three solved rungs; source-selected rational parameters; orders 1–3 vanish while order 4 may remain.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational/Taylor coefficient algebra.

**Checks in the source:** Each cancellation and raised vanishing order are asserted; omission of each rung leaves its coefficient nonzero.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. This scalar correction model is not the full nonlinear PDE iteration.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 19, Failed: 0; 1.22 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 19, Failed: 0; compile 1.30 s, run 0.21 s). <a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-residual-order-n"></a>

## Finite-order background residual recursion

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_residual_order_n.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_residual_order_n.esk#L1). SHA-256: `6e3ebda54051e7da69aa165959e5866cfd706f8edc99b36b2107365427f22c81`.

**Published result:** Section 5 of the reference construction, (5.1)–(5.6): with λ_n = 2nh every field coefficient is a formal series in q^{2h}; at each order the coefficients solve a linear system whose operator is the same at every order and whose source comes from lower orders (Proposition 5.3's induction). The program mechanizes that algebraic skeleton on a scalar model: substituting the order-N truncation, orders 0..N−1 of the residual vanish exactly and order N is the background residual beyond leading order.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Check lower-order cancellation in a finite formal expansion.

**Implemented algorithm:** Apply a fixed linear correction operator to known lower-order forcing; compare Taylor coefficients with derivative-n/factorial extraction.

**Domain and parameters:** N=4 in the supplied recursion and rational X samples; deliberately perturbed correction orders 0,2,3.

**Arithmetic:** Exact Taylor-coefficient/rational equality checks.

**Checks in the source:** Orders below N cancel, the order-N residual remains nonzero generally, extraction routes agree and perturbations reintroduce exactly their order.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. Finite truncation does not establish convergence or cancellation to infinitely many orders.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 8, Failed: 0; 1.52 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 8, Failed: 0; compile 1.93 s, run 0.20 s). CTest: `ns_residual_order_n_vanishes_jit` Passed (1.55 s), `ns_residual_order_n_vanishes_aot` Passed (2.29 s). Verdict line: `RESULT: ALL PASS`.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-similarity-scales"></a>

## Similarity coordinates and fitted scale laws

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_similarity_scales.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_similarity_scales.esk#L1). SHA-256: `3d5c00c6aa36d2a01aab06b7cde67775603073d54df9d01383447744b1c2bd7b`.

**Published result:** Sections 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 of the reference construction: with τ = 1 − t, A = 1/2 + h, D = 1/2 − h and similarity coordinates τ = q(1 − η²), z = q^D η, X = r²/(2q), the concentrating core has l_r ~ τ^{1/2}, l_z ~ τ^{1/2−h}, sup|u_θ|, sup|u_z| ~ τ^{−1/2−h}, sup|u_r| ~ τ^{−1/2}, and core kinetic energy ~ τ^{1/2−3h}; the background's momentum residual alone diverges like τ^{−(1+A)}, which is why the construction adds oscillatory pulses. The program builds an ansatz of that form and measures the exponents.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Differentiate the implicit similarity-coordinate construction and inspect scaling.

**Implemented algorithm:** Build the self-similar axisymmetric ansatz, differentiate q’s implicit solve, fit scale exponents and evaluate core energy/physical residual scaling.

**Domain and parameters:** τ=1−t, h=0.005=1/200, A=1/2+h, D=1/2−h; source-defined coordinate samples over six decades in τ.

**Arithmetic:** AD and floating-point fitted/physical quantities; source-specific tolerance comparisons.

**Checks in the source:** Incompressibility/pressure/coordinate relations and fitted energy/residual exponents are checked on the selected samples.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. Fitted or sampled exponent behavior is distinguished from an exact general asymptotic proof.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-stress-cone"></a>

## Admissible stress cone and profile tests

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_stress_cone.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_stress_cone.esk#L1). SHA-256: `9f42d15e596b5ddd5bcde8624f6b3599a439834dffec0624f8a939f994f57e4c`.

**Published result:** Section 4.3 of the reference construction, Lemma 4.5 and (4.20)–(4.23), with Appendix C: the annular stress must lie in the positive span of the two covariance directions; with t_s = −b_s/a, v_s = a(1 + t_s²), P_c, J_c as in (4.20), the admissible cone is P_c > 2, v_s > 2 and v_s < U(P_c, J_c), and Lemma 4.5 replaces the square root in U by the polynomial test P_c > v_s, (v_s − 2)J_c² < 2(P_c − v_s)², with a uniform threshold P_K on compact parameter sets. The program decides the cone by exact rational sign tests and places a constructed stress inside it.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Domain and parameters:** Source-selected rational profile/radius samples, positive rescalings and relaxed connecting-interval cone cases.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational signs/integration and explicit sampled checks.

**Checks in the source:** Cone equivalence tests, homogeneity, constructed-stress acceptance and nonpositive/transverse-heavy rejection are asserted.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. Acceptance on sampled radii must not be rewritten as an unchecked all-radius analytic bound.

<a id="mathematics-navier-stokes-viscosity-scaling"></a>

## Viscosity rescaling of an AD residual

Source: [mathematics_navier_stokes_viscosity_scaling.esk](../examples/mathematics_navier_stokes_viscosity_scaling.esk#L1). SHA-256: `abea7eaed518f1086cca52127da298fac84a25cb4e17a413854390b921ae257b`.

**Published result:** Section 10.4 of the reference construction, (10.22)–(10.23): if (u, p, f) solves the forced equations with viscosity 1, then u_ν(x, t) = √ν u(x/√ν, t), p_ν(x, t) = ν p(x/√ν, t), f_ν(x, t) = √ν f(x/√ν, t) solve them with viscosity ν, with ‖u_ν(t)‖₂² = ν^{5/2}‖u(t)‖₂² and ν‖∇u_ν‖₂² = ν^{5/2}‖∇u‖₂²; this transports the ν = 1 construction to every ν > 0. The program checks the rescaling identity for the full momentum residual, and the energy and dissipation scalings on a scaled grid, on an explicit divergence-free polynomial field, exactly at rational ν with rational square roots.

**References:**

- OpenAI, "Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes" (2026; the PDF carries no date line, the year is the one the program headers give). Theorem 1.1 constructs, for every viscosity ν > 0, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a smooth solution of the forced incompressible equations, starting from rest, whose kinetic energy stays bounded while its velocity becomes unbounded as t ↑ 1. <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf>

**Purpose:** Verify the residual, energy and dissipation rescaling on explicit fields.

**Implemented algorithm:** Assemble time/advection/Laplacian/pressure derivatives by AD for u=(1+t)(y²z,z²x,x²y), p=xyz+tx²; rescale fields and grids.

**Domain and parameters:** ν=1/4,1,9/16,25/9,4 with rational square roots; ν=2 as an irrational numerical case.

**Arithmetic:** Source asserts rational exact equalities for the rational cases; the ν=2 residual check uses 1e-9 tolerance.

**Checks in the source:** Divergence, residual identity and discrete ν^(5/2) energy/dissipation scaling are checked; omitted velocity/pressure factors fail.

**Limits:** Checks the stated finite model of one step of the reference construction; it does not reproduce the construction's analytic estimates, and nothing here is a machine proof of Theorem 1.1. Discrete quadrature/scaled-grid identities are not a new continuum integration theorem.

<a id="mathematics-presheaf-topos-internal-logic"></a>

## Internal logic of finite presheaf categories

Source: [mathematics_presheaf_topos_internal_logic.esk](../examples/mathematics_presheaf_topos_internal_logic.esk#L1). SHA-256: `11fdc767fc44cda5f0be5a43a347e44463caa810b37d3634905d3c77110163b8`.

**Published result:** In a presheaf topos Set^{C^op} the subobject classifier Ω assigns to c the set of sieves on c, exponentials are Y^X(c) = Hom(y(c) × X, Y), Ω is an internal Heyting algebra, and Lawvere–Tierney topologies correspond bijectively to Grothendieck topologies on C (Mac Lane–Moerdijk I.4, I.6, III.5, Theorem V.1.2). The program constructs each on small categories and checks the universal properties by counting both sides.

**References:**

- S. Mac Lane, I. Moerdijk, Sheaves in Geometry and Logic, Springer (1992). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- P. T. Johnstone, Sketches of an Elephant, Oxford (2002). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- F. W. Lawvere, "Quantifiers and sheaves" (1970). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Construct classifiers, exponentials and local operators as finite data.

**Implemented algorithm:** Enumerate sieves, subpresheaves and natural maps, construct exponentials and Heyting operations, and enumerate Grothendieck/Lawvere–Tierney topologies.

**Domain and parameters:** Walking arrow, pseudocircle, commutative square and BZ/2; explicitly supplied finite presheaves.

**Arithmetic:** Exact finite set enumeration and truth-table comparisons.

**Checks in the source:** Classifier bijections/pullbacks, exponential adjunction counts, Heyting laws/non-Boolean examples and 4/16/2 topology counts are checked.

**Limits:** The complete walking-arrow local-operator enumeration certifies that finite case; broader universal-property statements are restricted to the constructed inputs/cited theory.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 9, Failed: 0; 4.92 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 9, Failed: 0; compile 8.82 s, run 0.57 s). <a id="mathematics-sheafification-descent-kan"></a>

## Sheafification, reflector and Kan descent

Source: [mathematics_sheafification_descent_kan.esk](../examples/mathematics_sheafification_descent_kan.esk#L1). SHA-256: `72aae0f72e6bb160b435055a394c7cd2f9651f72b7d8a9ba588786d291684a49`.

**Published result:** Sheafification a = (−)⁺⁺ is left adjoint to the inclusion of sheaves (Mac Lane–Moerdijk Theorem III.5.1), and the sheaf condition for a covering sieve says that F(U) is the limit of F over the sieve — equivalently, the right Kan extension of F restricted to the sieve (Johnstone C2.2; Lurie 6.2.2). The program verifies the Grothendieck axioms for the canonical topology on two finite sites, counts matching families, computes the plus construction twice, and checks the reflector's universal property and the Kan-extension form of descent by counting.

**References:**

- S. Mac Lane, I. Moerdijk, Sheaves in Geometry and Logic, Springer (1992). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- P. T. Johnstone, Sketches of an Elephant, Oxford (2002), C2.2. (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Annals of Mathematics Studies 170, Princeton University Press (2009). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- M. C. McCord, "Singular homology groups and homotopy groups of finite topological spaces", Duke Math. J. 33 (1966). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. A. Barmak, Algebraic Topology of Finite Topological Spaces and Applications, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 2032, Springer (2011). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Compare finite-site plus construction with matching-family Kan limits.

**Implemented algorithm:** Enumerate covering sieves and finite matching families, apply plus twice, build comma-category limits and count natural maps into sheaves.

**Domain and parameters:** Pseudocircle site with 6 opens and pseudo-2-sphere site with 9 opens; constant, locally constant and nonseparated set presheaves.

**Arithmetic:** Exact finite sets and enumeration/pruned-count cross-checks.

**Checks in the source:** Grothendieck axioms, separated/sheaf conditions, section counts, Kan/matching equality and selected reflector-adjunction counts are asserted.

**Limits:** The exhaustive site is finite; selected adjunction counts must not be promoted to a proof for arbitrary infinite sites or all presheaves.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 10, Failed: 0; 8.15 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 10, Failed: 0; compile 19.4 s, run 1.10 s). <a id="mathematics-stacks-nonabelian-descent"></a>

## Torsors and nonabelian descent on finite spaces

Source: [mathematics_stacks_nonabelian_descent.esk](../examples/mathematics_stacks_nonabelian_descent.esk#L1). SHA-256: `ec081828506dfeb2f49624d1dc0d6433da10330f60ae1e7d9a0690b00833d097`.

**Published result:** G-torsors on a space are classified by nonabelian H¹, i.e. Hom(π₁, G)/G with automorphisms the centralizers (Giraud), and the torsor stack satisfies descent along covers whose intersections are contractible (Hollander; Lurie 6.5.3–6.5.4). The program computes the groupoid of G-torsors on finite-space models of the circle, the torus and the Klein bottle directly as Fun(X, BG), checks Čech descent on covers by maximal opens, and shows that the Klein bottle separates D₄ from Q₈ (20 against 16 torsor classes) where the torus does not.

**References:**

- J. Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne, Grundlehren 179, Springer (1971). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- S. Hollander, "A homotopy theory for stacks", Israel J. Math. 163 (2008). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. F. Jardine, Local Homotopy Theory, Springer (2015), Ch. 9. (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Annals of Mathematics Studies 170, Princeton University Press (2009). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- M. C. McCord, "Singular homology groups and homotopy groups of finite topological spaces", Duke Math. J. 33 (1966). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. A. Barmak, Algebraic Topology of Finite Topological Spaces and Applications, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 2032, Springer (2011). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J.-P. Serre, Trees, I.5. (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Compare torsor groupoids and descent on torus/Klein-bottle models.

**Implemented algorithm:** Backtrack group labels on Hasse edges with path relations, gauge-fix a spanning tree, quotient by conjugation and compute centralizers/Cech descent data.

**Domain and parameters:** Source-supplied finite spaces and six finite groups, including S₃, D₄ and Q₈; Klein bottle as a twisted finite product.

**Arithmetic:** Exact group-table enumeration and rational groupoid cardinalities.

**Checks in the source:** Cover conditions, bundle/class/automorphism counts and descent agreement are asserted; D₄ and Q₈ differ in Klein-bottle class counts despite equal cardinality.

**Limits:** Finite torsor groupoids are calculated rather than a general stack theory solver; the underlying finite model identifications use the cited topology.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-turaev-viro-cyclotomic"></a>

## Exact cyclotomic Turaev–Viro state sums

Source: [mathematics_turaev_viro_cyclotomic.esk](../examples/mathematics_turaev_viro_cyclotomic.esk#L1). SHA-256: `9d9112a7cec9c780980892c1ecf7545aea2350d3953af7e5edc7580d2e197fc4`.

**Published result:** Turaev and Viro (1992) define 3-manifold invariants as state sums of quantum 6j-symbols; with Kauffman–Lins recoupling data at A = ζ_{4r} the state sum is TV_r(M) = η^V Σ ∏Δ ∏θ⁻¹ ∏Tet. TV_r is the squared norm of the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant (Roberts 1995), TV_r(T³) counts simple objects of the Drinfeld centre ((r−1)² for SU(2)_{r−2}), and at level one (r = 3) the theory is the double semion, the Z/2 Dijkgraaf–Witten theory with the nontrivial cocycle. The program evaluates the state sums exactly in cyclotomic fields.

**References:**

- V. G. Turaev, O. Y. Viro, "State sum invariants of 3-manifolds and quantum 6j-symbols", Topology 31 (1992). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- L. H. Kauffman, S. L. Lins, Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds, Annals of Mathematics Studies 134 (1994). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Roberts, "Skein theory and Turaev-Viro invariants", Topology 34 (1995). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- M. Levin, X.-G. Wen (2005), string-net models (the double semion). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Evaluate recoupling state sums and compare selected triangulations and theories.

**Implemented algorithm:** Build cyclotomic polynomials/field inverses, quantum integers, theta/tetrahedral nets and admissible edge-coloring sums.

**Domain and parameters:** A=ζ₄r; r=3,4,5 on supplied S³/RP³/T³ and lens complexes, with specified level restrictions per comparison.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational cyclotomic field arithmetic.

**Checks in the source:** Quantum relations, alternative triangulation agreement, selected homeomorphic lens values, double-semion comparison and torus counts 4/9/16 are asserted.

**Limits:** Finite comparisons cover only the listed triangulations; Pachner-move invariance and normalization follow the cited theory.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 9, Failed: 0; 10.7 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 9, Failed: 0; compile 23.1 s, run 2.62 s). CTest: `tv_turaev_viro_cyclotomic_jit` Passed (23.1 s), `tv_turaev_viro_cyclotomic_aot` Passed (28.8 s). Verdict line: `RESULT: ALL PASS`.

```text
  TV_4 separates L(5,1) from L(5,2)?  TV_5?  TV_4 separates L(7,1) from L(7,2)? = (#f #t #f)
  TV_3, TV_4, TV_5 of T^3 = (4 9 16)
```

<a id="mathematics-two-descent-cech-nerves"></a>

## Cech nerves and 2-descent

Source: [mathematics_two_descent_cech_nerves.esk](../examples/mathematics_two_descent_cech_nerves.esk#L1). SHA-256: `0a7ac6f1b5d1d364746801aa5f985fcc3b3da530ae55e804521f461bc7208985`.

**Published result:** Descent for ∞-sheaves along Čech nerves and hypercovers (Lurie 6.5.3–6.5.4; Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen 2004) and the nerve theorem (Björner; McCord): when every component of every intersection of a cover is contractible, the Čech nerve is weakly equivalent to the space, so mapping spaces into a 2-group's classifying space have equal homotopy cardinality on both. The program computes these cardinalities (Faria Martins–Porter) on finite-space covers and exhibits a cover of the pseudo-2-sphere where descent fails for 2-types but not for 1-types.

**References:**

- J. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Annals of Mathematics Studies 170, Princeton University Press (2009). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- D. Dugger, S. Hollander, D. C. Isaksen, "Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves", Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 136 (2004). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. F. Jardine, Local Homotopy Theory, Springer (2015), Ch. 9. (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Faria Martins, T. Porter, "On Yetter's invariant and an extension of the Dijkgraaf-Witten invariant to categorical groups", Theory Appl. Categ. 18 (2007). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- A. Björner, "Nerves, fibers and homotopy groups", J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 102 (2003). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- M. C. McCord, "Singular homology groups and homotopy groups of finite topological spaces", Duke Math. J. 33 (1966). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. A. Barmak, Algebraic Topology of Finite Topological Spaces and Applications, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 2032, Springer (2011). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Expose descent failures visible to 2-types but invisible to 1-types.

**Implemented algorithm:** Construct intersection-component Cech nerves through their 3-skeleton, compute crossed-module mapping counts and compare order-complex and fibration routes.

**Domain and parameters:** Pseudocircle, torus, Klein-bottle and pseudo-2-sphere covers; supplied finite 2-groups and Z/2,Z/3 targets.

**Arithmetic:** Exact finite incidence, modular Smith-form counts and rational normalizations.

**Checks in the source:** Leray-cover agreements and the non-Leray sphere discrepancy are asserted; T³ uses the enumerated 3-skeleton needed for these 2-type targets.

**Limits:** The intersection-component nerve used here is not the full topological Cech simplicial object in every context; its contractible-component hypotheses and finite target scope are explicit.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 12, Failed: 0; 45.5 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 12, Failed: 0; compile 19.6 s, run 27.4 s). CTest: `descent_two_descent_cech_nerves_jit` Passed (40.2 s), `descent_two_descent_cech_nerves_aot` Passed (42.7 s). Verdict line: `RESULT: ALL PASS`.

```text
  pseudo-2-sphere: Map(C(U), BG) and Map(S^2, BG) for BZ/2, K(Z/2,2), Z/2->Z/2 = ((1/2 2 1) (1/2 4 2))
PASS: descent failure is invisible to the 1-type BZ/2 (1/2 on both sides, pi_1 S^2 = 0) and visible to K(Z/2,2) (nerve 2, space 4) and to the split 2-type (1 against 2)
```

<a id="mathematics-two-groups-postnikov"></a>

## Crossed-module nerves and Postnikov data

Source: [mathematics_two_groups_postnikov.esk](../examples/mathematics_two_groups_postnikov.esk#L1). SHA-256: `506ec63d21f893faf59f35ed1e17a65ecb2faf48d1a601ef00bc150b0a8c0f62`.

**Published result:** Strict 2-groups are crossed modules (Whitehead 1949); the classifying space of a crossed module d: M → N is a 2-type with π₁ = coker d and π₂ = ker d (Brown–Higgins–Sivera §2.5), classified by π₁, π₂ and a k-invariant in H³(π₁; π₂) (Baez–Lauda §8), with Z/4 → Z/4 (sign action) realizing the nontrivial class for π₁ = π₂ = Z/2. The program enumerates the nerves (Duskin's description) and shows that cohomology in degree 2 separates 2-types with equal homotopy groups.

**References:**

- J. H. C. Whitehead, "Combinatorial homotopy II", Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 55 (1949). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- R. Brown, P. J. Higgins, R. Sivera, Nonabelian Algebraic Topology, EMS (2011). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Duskin, "Simplicial matrices and the nerves of weak n-categories I", Theory Appl. Categ. 9 (2002). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. C. Baez, A. D. Lauda, "Higher-dimensional algebra V: 2-groups", Theory Appl. Categ. 12 (2004). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. P. May, Simplicial Objects in Algebraic Topology (1967), §23. (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Distinguish 2-types with identical π₁ and π₂ using k-sensitive cohomology.

**Implemented algorithm:** Check crossed-module/Peiffer laws, enumerate edge/triangle-labeled nerve simplices, check face identities and compute integral/mod-2 complexes.

**Domain and parameters:** Finite abelian crossed modules including Z/2→1,1→Z/2,Z/2→Z/2 and Z/4→Z/4 with trivial/sign action; source-defined low degrees.

**Arithmetic:** Exact integer and finite-field linear algebra.

**Checks in the source:** Kernel/cokernel homotopy sizes, cohomology dimensions, nontrivial-twist distinction and dropped-tetrahedron-equation negative controls are asserted.

**Limits:** Finite-degree computations distinguish these presentations; equivalence of entire 2-types invokes the cited crossed-module/Postnikov theory.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 18, Failed: 0; 21.0 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 18, Failed: 0; compile 6.89 s, run 12.7 s). CTest: `hocolim_two_groups_postnikov_jit` Passed (19.6 s), `hocolim_two_groups_postnikov_aot` Passed (22.3 s), `vm_mathematics_two_groups_postnikov` Passed (74.2 s). Verdict line: `RESULT: ALL PASS`.

<a id="mathematics-yetter-three-torus-finite-model"></a>

## Yetter invariants on the 64-point torus

Source: [mathematics_yetter_three_torus_finite_model.esk](../examples/mathematics_yetter_three_torus_finite_model.esk#L1). SHA-256: `3378acb1aa13827bc82f111bfd7a07049f902cf4115d09cf8f50866a2c702b75`.

**Published result:** Yetter's 2-group invariants are topological, so on any triangulation of T³ they must equal the values computed on the one-vertex six-tetrahedron triangulation in the sibling program. The program recomputes nine of them on the 384-tetrahedron order complex of the 64-point finite model of T³ (McCord), where brute-force enumeration (|N|^385 labellings) is out of reach and the 1-gauge reduction is used, and checks them against the Postnikov fibration formula.

**References:**

- D. N. Yetter, "TQFT's from homotopy 2-types", J. Knot Theory Ramifications 2 (1993). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- T. Porter, "Topological quantum field theories from homotopy n-types", J. London Math. Soc. 58 (1998). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Faria Martins, T. Porter, "On Yetter's invariant and an extension of the Dijkgraaf-Witten invariant to categorical groups", Theory Appl. Categ. 18 (2007). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- M. C. McCord, "Singular homology groups and homotopy groups of finite topological spaces", Duke Math. J. 33 (1966). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. A. Barmak, Algebraic Topology of Finite Topological Spaces and Applications, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 2032, Springer (2011). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Recompute 2-group invariants on a larger finite-space triangulation.

**Implemented algorithm:** Use spanning-tree holonomies, 1-gauge reduction, cached twisted Smith forms and independent fibration counts.

**Domain and parameters:** 64 vertices/448 edges/768 triangles/384 tetrahedra; nine supplied crossed modules; 8 or 27 holonomies.

**Arithmetic:** Exact integer/modular Smith forms and rational normalizations, including denominator factors 2³⁸⁴ or 3³⁸⁴.

**Checks in the source:** The nine stated invariants and two routes agree exactly; source checks twelve reused Smith forms and twisted-coefficient orders.

**Limits:** Avoids impossible brute-force edge enumeration using a source-derived gauge reduction; the reduction is checked against full enumeration in the sibling lens-space program, not here. The measured outcome below records the run time at the release SHA; the program's own wall-time and peak-memory report goes to the compiler measurement stream, not to this catalogue.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 11, Failed: 0; 99.4 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 11, Failed: 0; compile 14.5 s, run 48.6 s). <a id="mathematics-yetter-two-group-invariants"></a>

## Yetter state sums and Postnikov fibration

Source: [mathematics_yetter_two_group_invariants.esk](../examples/mathematics_yetter_two_group_invariants.esk#L1). SHA-256: `51777e8a49ad8535dea26ca65a9bc8c10f262fc287146a89087f5177720a065f`.

**Published result:** Yetter (1993) defines a 3-manifold invariant from a finite 2-group as a normalized count of simplicial maps into the nerve of the 2-group; Faria Martins and Porter (2007) identify it with the homotopy cardinality of the mapping space Map(X, BG), computable through the Postnikov fibration K(π₂, 2) → BG → Bπ₁ with the k-invariant as an obstruction and local coefficients twisted by π₁. The program computes both routes for six crossed modules on S³, RP³ and T³.

**References:**

- D. N. Yetter, "TQFT's from homotopy 2-types", J. Knot Theory Ramifications 2 (1993). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- T. Porter, "Topological quantum field theories from homotopy n-types", J. London Math. Soc. 58 (1998). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. Faria Martins, T. Porter, "On Yetter's invariant and an extension of the Dijkgraaf-Witten invariant to categorical groups", Theory Appl. Categ. 18 (2007). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. C. Baez, J. Dolan, "From finite sets to Feynman diagrams" (2001). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- J. C. Baez, A. D. Lauda, "Higher-dimensional algebra V: 2-groups", Theory Appl. Categ. 12 (2004). (as cited in the program's source comments)
- A. Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Cambridge University Press (2002). (as cited in the program's source comments)

**Purpose:** Compare explicit crossed-module state sums with mapping-space formulas.

**Implemented algorithm:** Gauge-fix edge labels, solve affine triangle equations by Smith forms and evaluate local-coefficient obstruction/fibration counts.

**Domain and parameters:** Supplied S³,RP³,T³ Delta-complexes and six crossed modules, including sign-action Z/4→Z/4 and Z/3→Z/2.

**Arithmetic:** Exact group labels, integer Smith forms and rational cardinalities.

**Checks in the source:** Presentation-equivalence cases, RP³ k-obstruction, twisted coefficient orders and independent counting-route equality are asserted.

**Limits:** Counts apply to these finite complexes/modules; general topological invariance and mapping-space interpretations use cited theorems.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

**Measured at `60f345def`** (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): native JIT **PASS** (Passed: 13, Failed: 0; 6.32 s); native AOT **PASS** (Passed: 13, Failed: 0; compile 10.6 s, run 1.30 s).
